name: Elite Dangerous

start.note: official Frontier launcher entry point; the game executable is not started separately

summary.ja: 公式ランチャーからゲーム本体まで動作。Mac の画面（VXRT_FLAT=1）では M1 Max・Low でゲーム中 約 52〜122 fps（メニューは 250〜330）、ヘッドセットでは片目 1700x1372 で 30〜35 fps 前後。キーボード・マウスはゲーム内で効き、DualSense は平面で確認（VR は未確認）。ランチャーはプレイヤーがサインインして PLAY を押す。
summary.en: Runs from the official launcher to the game. On the Mac's screen (VXRT_FLAT=1), about 52-122 fps in game on an M1 Max with graphics on Low (menus 250-330); in the headset, around 30-35 fps at 1700x1372 per eye. Keyboard and mouse work in game; a DualSense is checked flat (not yet in VR). The player signs in and presses PLAY in the launcher.

known_issues.summary: Run 20261018T205736Z-elite_dangerous-start verifies the blank-click fix. Before it, run 20261018T205445Z clicked the visually empty coordinate (700, 500), but VXRuntime's hyperlink hit rectangle extended from x=108 to x=780; the click incorrectly invoked HomeCreateAccountPage.OnTandC and exited at a null System.Object.ToString receiver. The hyperlink now gets a hit rectangle from GetTextExtentPoint32W. After the fix, the same click leaves the rendered Signup page open and the 40-second run completes: o1 exited_early=false, o10-o13 are 0, o14 first_problem=null. No credentials were entered and signup was not submitted. SteamVR was not reached (o2=null), and EliteDangerous64.exe did not launch. Actual clicks on the T&C/Privacy Policy glyphs have not been tested.

Run 20261018T193452Z-elite_dangerous-start confirms EDLaunch.exe reaches a usable WPF login screen without CLR exceptions, managed exceptions, native signals, or unimplemented calls. A dummy character entered through the watermark hit target updates the TextBoxText binding source. The official launcher still reports version 1.7.7036.1 requires update. No Frontier credentials were entered, no login was submitted, no update was started, and EliteDangerous64.exe was not launched; the game's D3D11/OpenVR/input/network path remains unmeasured until the user updates and signs in through the official launcher.

No credentials were entered and no login action was submitted. The run has no unimplemented calls, CLR exceptions, native signals, or first problem (o10-o14), but there is no SteamVR connection (o2=null, d3=false) and no game launch.

EDLaunch.exe is PE32/I386 but its CLR flags are IL-only and do not require 32-bit execution. It references .NET Framework 4.8/WPF assemblies; launcher support needs managed runtime behavior plus WPF desktop/UI APIs.

VXRuntime includes bounds-checked PE/ECMA-335 metadata, .resources and WPF BAML readers, a bounded CIL interpreter with managed objects, fields, delegates and method calls, and a built-in mscoree.dll _CorExeMain path. For EDLaunch.exe it validates app.baml and recursively resolves all 13 merged ResourceDictionary.Source references, including deferred dictionary-key records in ButtonStyles. Mapping BAML records into WPF types, constructing XAML object trees, the dispatcher and message loop remain incomplete.
The installed game executable is EliteDangerous64.exe. Its compatibility remains unknown until the official launcher can run.

Static imports from the x64 game include Direct3D 11, DXGI, OpenVR, DirectInput 8, XInput, WinHTTP and Winsock; D3D12 and Vulkan are not imported. Elite will first exercise the D3D11 path once the official launcher can run.
